events.transit.the_wrong_carriage.title: The Wrong End of the Train
events.transit.the_wrong_carriage.body: The seats here have headrests and nobody standing. Yours does not, and is four carriages back. The conductor has started at the far door and is working his way down, and he is not hurrying, which somehow makes it worse.
events.transit.the_wrong_carriage.out.se: He writes it out by hand, takes the money, and gives you a stub with a number on it. The seat is not better. Not having to think about it is.
events.transit.the_wrong_carriage.out.be: You explain. He looks at the ticket, looks at you, and decides that on balance he has had a long day too. He moves on.
events.transit.the_wrong_carriage.out.st: The story is fine until he asks one ordinary question about it, and then it is not. He does not raise his voice. He just waits while you rearrange it.
events.transit.the_wrong_carriage.out.sc: It gets loud, and it gets loud in front of forty people who now all know your face and what you sound like when cornered.
events.transit.the_wrong_carriage.choice: Move down before he gets here
events.transit.the_wrong_carriage.out.sl: You go the long way round through the buffet car and are in your own seat, breathing normally, by the time he reaches it.
events.transit.the_wrong_carriage.out.ca: He comes through the connecting door as you are going the other way, and there is nowhere in a corridor that width to look like you belong.
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.title: The Boarding Queue
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.body: A queue of freight, a queue of foot passengers, and a man with a clipboard who has already decided which one you are. The boat is a rust-streaked slab with the ramp down and its engines running. Nobody says how long the crossing takes. Everybody seems to know.
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.out.a_: A moulded bench, a strip light that does not turn off, and six hours of somebody else's radio. You are across, and that is the whole of it.
You know which bench now, and which end of the deck the wind does not reach. It is not comfort. It is competence.
Same bench, same strip light, same radio. You sleep through most of it out of practice rather than tiredness.
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.out.ro: The swell gets up somewhere in the middle and stays up. Nobody on the deck talks for the last three hours, on principle.
It rolls again, and knowing it is going to does not help in the slightest.
You spend the crossing on the outside rail, which is cold and wet and still the better option.
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.out.sl: A cabin the size of a cupboard, a door that locks, and eight hours of not being anywhere. It is the best money you have spent in a fortnight.
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.choice: Present your papers at the ramp
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.out.st: He reads two lines of it, stamps the third, and hands it back without looking up. You are on the manifest.
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.out.pu: You are moved out of the line and into an office with one chair in it, and the boat is loaded around the fact of you sitting there.
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.out.th: Yours are fine. The vehicle's are a different form, filed somewhere else, in a hand nobody can read. It sails anyway, and so do you, on an understanding.
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.choice: Lend a hand on the vehicle deck
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.out.pa: You spend the crossing chocking wheels and running chains with the drivers, and come off it fed, paid a little, and known to four people who do this route monthly.
events.transit.the_boarding_queue.out.se: Seven hours in a space with no daylight and a floor that moves. Nobody pays you and nobody asked you to be there.
